Alex Chen: Heads-up — started a quick cost vs latency sweep for ORD/AMS/SFO for next quarter commitments. Wanted to share initial numbers and get input on where we should bias reserved capacity.
Priya Patel: awesome, what metrics did you use? per-token cost including egress?
Alex Chen: per-GPU-hour normalized to our p99 token distribution + estimated egress heavier for AMS -> EU customers. Also included spot interrupt rates for SFO.
Jamie O'Neill: can you paste the raw numbers? even a tiny table is fine.
Alex Chen: sure, pasted the sample rows below (rounded):
```
region | gpu_hour_cost | effective_cost_per_token | p99_latency_ms | spot_interrupt
ORD    | 3.05          | 0.00072                  | 36             | 1.2%           
AMS    | 3.40          | 0.00078                  | 42             | 0.6%           
SFO    | 4.10          | 0.00095                  | 48             | 6.8%           
```
Alex Chen: notes — AMS has slightly higher unit cost but better proximity to EU customers (lower e2e latency than ORD->EU). SFO cheaper for US-west users but spot instability is a problem for Dedicated pools.
Leo Martinez: what's the delta when we enable quantized kernels (int8) vs fp16? any region-specific perf changes?
Alex Chen: quantization reduces effective_cost_per_token by ~12% across regions; p99 improves 3-6ms; kernel availability tested on ORD/AMS fine, SFO had some older CUDA drivers causing a fallback but still net win.
Maria Gomez: what about cross-region egress billing when routing EU traffic to ORD vs AMS? that kills the cost if we do a lot of model hops, right?
Alex Chen: yes — if we route EU-routed requests to ORD for model variants, egress adds ~0.00015 per token in our baseline for high-volume flows. If we keep EU-serving in AMS, we avoid that.
Priya Patel: TL;DR recommendation?
Alex Chen: initial recommendation: keep baseline canary density in AMS for EU SLOs (small reserved pool ~20% of EU traffic), move majority of US-east workload to ORD reserved commitments (60% of reserved commits), retain SFO spot-backed burst capacity for west coast but not for Reserved/Dedicated primary.
Jamie O'Neill: what about failover? if AMS saturates, fallback to ORD will add latency and egress — acceptable?
Leo Martinez: we can set policy: prefer local region, failover to ORD only for non-interactive batches or lower-priority routes. For strict p99 chat requests we don't failover.
Maria Gomez: ops question — will our autoscaler respect regional reserved pools or will it pull from global shared capacity? need to ensure Dedicated usage honors billing buckets.
Alex Chen: autoscaler already has a region affinity flag in rollout v0.9.3. We'll lock dedicated pool to region for the reserved capacity groups. Only global preemptible/spot can pull cross-region.
infra-bot: Deploybot: rollout v0.9.3 to infra-autoscaler completed by CI at 2024-05-01T18:02:13Z (:white_check_mark:)
Priya Patel: can you run a cost-projection script for 12 months with those mixes? use commitments=ORD:60%, AMS:25%, SFO:15% with burst from spot.
Alex Chen: putting the query here to run in billing playbook — feel free to tweak:
```
# pseudo-SQL
SELECT region, SUM(gpu_hours * price_per_hour * (1 - quant_saving)) as monthly_cost
FROM forecast
WHERE commit_mix = 'ord60_ams25_sfo15' AND quant = 'int8'
GROUP BY region;
```
Jamie O'Neill: action items?
Alex Chen: 1) Priya — run full 12-month projection with traffic seasonality (due EOD tomorrow). 2) Leo — validate driver/kernel compatibility on SFO fleet (ETA 48h). 3) Maria — update autoscaler policy to hard-affinity reserved groups (PR draft). 4) Jamie — prepare brief for finance on commitment proposal and expected savings vs current on-demand mix.
Priya Patel: will do the projection, I'll include sensitivity: +-10% traffic, +-20% spot interrupts.
Leo Martinez: starting kernel checks now, will post logs.
Maria Gomez: drafting PR, will add test harness.
Jamie O'Neill: I'll coordinate with finance and get a preliminary commit ask ready for next Thurs.
Alex Chen: thanks y'all. If anyone spots obvious blind spots (network egress cost leaking, interconnect pricing, or reserved SKU mismatches) shout here.
Priya Patel: one more ask — can we run a latency SLO sim for ORD->EU vs AMS baseline? want concrete p99 numbers for user impact.
Alex Chen: yes, I'll queue a synthetic run against both region endpoints overnight and post results in the thread.
infra-bot: Monitor: synthetic-latency-job queued (job-id: syn-2145679)
Maria Gomez: noted, will include a comment in the PR linking to job-id.
Jamie O'Neill: great thread.
Alex Chen: wrapping: plan to lock commit allocations after Priya's projection and finance sign-off. Expect a follow-up thread with the exact SKU and term lengths. :thumbsup:
